label: External (library-backed) JavaScript UDF
type: a SQL++ user-defined function (n1ql:create-function, LANGUAGE JAVASCRIPT) that references a named function inside a js-udf:udf-library, as against js-udf:sql-managed-udf, whose JavaScript body is stored inline by the function definition itself with no separate library.
recurrence_note: 4 files, `divergent` - discount rejected, raw count stands.
evidence: If you have created a JavaScript function in a JavaScript library, you must create a SQL++ user-defined function to reference it.
If the JavaScript library is scoped, create a scoped user-defined function in the same scope as the library.
relates_to_competency_question: What is the difference between a UDF that references a library and one whose JavaScript is stored inline?
